title: Reported PHP Flaw Disables TLS for Mixed-Case HTTPS Schemes
summary: A reported PHP vulnerability causes the HTTP and FTP stream wrappers to treat mixed-case schemes such as HTTPS://, httpS:// and FTPS:// as plaintext HTTP/FTP, silently disabling TLS and potentially exposing credentials, cookies, POST bodies and FTP logins. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-128064 \(GHSA-f6gg-rchx-xw8j\) with a CVSS 4.0 score of 8.2, and fixes are available in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0. PHP 8.1 and earlier are end-of-life and will not receive a fix, so affected users must lower-case URL schemes themselves; the claim that the bug went unnoticed for 20 years comes from the source and has not been independently verified here.
